97.h: 2 - Abū Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah ibn Qays * (س)
97.t:
ibn ʿAdī, Abū Ḥudhāfah al-Sahmī.
One of the foremost converts, he emigrated to Abyssinia, and the Prophet ﷺ dispatched him as a messenger to Khosrow (3).
He has a small amount of narration. ⟦2:11⟧
He went out to Syria as a fighter, and was taken captive at Caesarea; they brought him to their tyrant, who tried to draw him away from his religion, but he was not led astray.
Narrating from him: سليمان بن يسار، وأبو وائل، ومسعود بن الحكم، وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن.
al-Bukhārī said: His hadith is mursal (مرسل).
Abū Bakr ibn al-Barqī said: What was memorised from him is three hadiths that are not connected.
Abū Saʿīd ibn Yūnus and Ibn Mandah said: He witnessed Badr.
Yūnus: عن الزهري، عن أبي سلمة: that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah stood to pray and recited aloud, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “O Ibn Ḥudhāfah! Do not make me hear, and let Allah hear (1).”
محمد بن عمرو: عن عمر بن الحكم بن ثوبان، أن أبا سعيد قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a detachment, with ʿAlqamah ibn Mujazziz over them, and I was among them.
We set out, and when we were part of the way along the road, a group asked his permission, and he permitted them, and appointed ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah over them. He was one of the people of Badr, and he had a sense of humour. While we were on the road, the men lit a fire to warm themselves by it and to prepare a meal of theirs on it, when he said: Do I not have your hearing and obedience?
They said: Indeed.
He said: Then I command you by my right and your obedience to leap into this fire.
Some people stood up and girded themselves (2), ⟦2:12⟧ until, when he thought they were about to fall into it, he said: Hold back, I was only joking with you.
When they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they mentioned that to him, and he said: “Whoever commands you to disobedience, do not obey him (1).”
Abū Yaʿlā included it in his Musnad.
Ibn al-Munkadir narrated it from ʿUmar ibn al-Ḥakam, and made it mursal (مرسل).
Thābit al-Bunānī narrated from Anas:
that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Ask me.”
A man said: Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?
He said: “Your father is Ḥudhāfah” (2). ⟦2:13⟧
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Jumaḥī: حدثنا عبد العزيز القسملي، حدثنا ضرار بن عمرو، عن أبي رافع، قال:
ʿUmar sent an army to the Romans, and they captured ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥudhāfah and took him to their king, saying: This one is from the companions of Muḥammad.
He said: Would you convert to Christianity, and I will give you half of my kingdom?
He said: If you gave me all that you own and all the kingdom of the Arabs, I would not turn back from the religion of Muḥammad for the blink of an eye.
He said: Then I will kill you.
He said: You and that.
So he ordered him to be crucified, and said to the archers: Shoot near his body.
All the while he offered it to him and he refused. Then he took him down and called for a cauldron, into which water was poured until it boiled fiercely, and he called for two Muslim prisoners, ordered one of them, and he was thrown into it, while he offered Christianity to him and he refused, then he wept.
It was said to the king: He wept.
He thought that he had become anxious, and said: Bring him back.
What made you weep?
He said: I said: It is one soul that will be thrown in now and be gone, and I wished that I had as many souls as the hairs of my head to be thrown into the Fire for Allah.
The tyrant said to him: Would you kiss my head, and I will release you?
ʿAbd Allāh said to him: And all the prisoners?
He said: Yes.
So he kissed his head, and returned with the prisoners to ʿUmar and informed him of his account.
ʿUmar said: It is a duty upon every Muslim to kiss the head of Ibn Ḥudhāfah, and I will begin.
Then he kissed his head (1). ⟦2:14⟧
al-Walīd ibn Muslim: حدثنا أبو عمرو، ومالك بن أنس:
that the people of Caesarea captured Ibn Ḥudhāfah, and their king ordered that he be tested with various things, which he endured, then they placed him in a house with wine and pork for three days, and he did not eat.
They looked in on him, and said to the king:
His neck has bent; if you bring him out, well, otherwise he will die.
He brought him out and said: What kept you from eating and drinking?
He said: Necessity had made them lawful for me, but I disliked to give you cause to gloat over Islam.
He said: Then kiss my head, and I will free a hundred prisoners for you.
He said: As for this, yes.
He kissed his head, and he freed a hundred for him, and let him go.
Ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated the story of Ibn Ḥudhāfah, saying:
al-Walīd ibn Muḥammad narrated to us: that Ibn Ḥudhāfah was captured ..., then he mentioned the story at length, and in it he released three hundred prisoners for him, and gave him a reward of thirty thousand dinars, thirty maidservants and thirty manservants.
Perhaps this king had become Muslim in secret, and his excessive honouring of Ibn Ḥudhāfah indicates that.
The same is said of Heraclius when he proposed to his people entering the religion, and when he feared them he said:
I was only testing your firmness in your religion.
Whoever becomes Muslim inwardly in this way, deliverance from eternal abiding in the Fire is hoped for him, since some faith has come about in his inner self (1). What is feared is only that he has submitted to Islam and to the Messenger and believed that both are true, while remaining on a valid religion, so you see him revering both religions, as many nominal Muslims of the government bureaus have done (2); this does not benefit him ⟦2:15⟧ Islam until he disavows polytheism.
Ibn Ḥudhāfah died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān - may Allah be pleased with them.

98.h: 3 - Abū Rāfiʿ, the client (المولى) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ * (ع)
98.t:
From the Copts of Egypt.
It is said: His name is Ibrāhīm.
It is said: Aslam.
He was a slave of al-ʿAbbās, who gave him to the Prophet ﷺ, and when the Prophet ﷺ was given the good news of al-ʿAbbās's conversion to Islam, he freed him.
He narrated a number of hadiths.
Narrating from him: his son ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, his grandson al-Faḍl ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, أبو سعيد المقبري، وعمرو بن الشريد، وجماعة كثيرة.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn also narrated from him, though it seems he did not hear from him directly.
He witnessed the Battle of Uḥud and the Trench, and he was a man of knowledge and excellence.
He died in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿAlī.
It is said: He died in Kufa in the year 40 (may Allah be pleased with him).
It is said: He made a bequest to ʿAlī, and ʿAlī used to pay zakat on the property of the sons of Abū Rāfiʿ while they were orphans.
Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj said: I was informed that he was a Copt. ⟦2:16⟧
Shuʿbah: عن الحكم، عن ابن أبي رافع، عن أبيه:
that the Prophet ﷺ sent a man to collect charity, and he said to Abū Rāfiʿ: Come with me, and we will take a share of it.
I said: Not until I ask permission of the Messenger of Allah.
So I asked his permission, and he said: “O Abū Rāfiʿ, the client (المولى) of a people is one of them, and charity is not lawful for us (1).”
Sulaymān ibn Yasār said:
Abū Rāfiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not order me to stop at al-Abṭaḥ when he left Minā, but I came and stopped, and he came and stopped (2).

99.h: 4 - Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān Abū Yaḥyā al-Namarī * (ع)
99.t:
Of al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ.
He is known as al-Rūmī because he stayed among the Romans for a time.
He was from the people of al-Jazīrah, taken captive from the village of Nineveh, in the districts of ⟦2:17⟧ Mosul.
His father or his uncle had been an agent of Khosrow, then he was brought to Mecca, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān al-Qurashī al-Taymī bought him.
It is said: Rather, he fled and came to Mecca and made a pact of alliance with Ibn Judʿān.
He was among the great foremost converts and the Badrīs (البدري).
Narrating from him: بنوه؛ حبيب، وزياد (1)، وحمزة؛ وسعيد بن المسيب، وكعب الحبر، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وآخرون.
He narrated a limited number of hadiths, which they included for him in the Six Books (الكتب الستة).
He was a man of excellence, held in great esteem, and had several children.
When ʿUmar was stabbed, he appointed him to lead the Muslims in prayer until the people of the Council agreed upon an imam.
He was described as generous and open-handed (may Allah be pleased with him).
He died in Medina, in Shawwāl, in the year 38, and he was among those who withdrew from the strife and attended to his own affairs (may Allah be pleased with him).
The hadith master (الحافظ) Ibn ʿAsākir said: Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān ibn Mālik ibn ʿAbd (2) ʿAmr ibn ʿUqayl ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Yaḥyā - and it is said Abū Ghassān - al-Namarī, al-Rūmī, al-Badrī, al-Muhājirī.
Narrating from him: بنوه، وابن عمر، وجابر، وابن المسيب، وعبيد بن عمير، وابن أبي ليلى، وبنوه الثمانية: عثمان، وصيفي، وحمزة، وسعد، وعباد، وحبيب، وصالح، ومحمد. ⟦2:18⟧
Ibn Saʿd mentioned him and listed his lineage up to Aslam ibn Aws Manāh ibn al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ, of Rabīʿah, confederate of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān al-Taymī al-Qurashī.
His mother was Salmā bint Qaʿīd.
He was a reddish man, very red, not tall.
Shabāb (1) mentioned his lineage up to al-Namir, with additional forefathers and others omitted.
Aḥmad ibn al-Barqī did likewise.
From Ḥamzah ibn Ṣuhayb, from his father, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ gave me the patronymic (الكنية) Abū Yaḥyā (2).
From Ṣayfī ibn Ṣuhayb, from his father, who said:
I accompanied the Prophet ﷺ before revelation came to him (3).
And from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmmār, from his father:
ʿAmmār said: I met Ṣuhayb at the door of the house of al-Arqam, in which was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so we entered, and he presented Islam to us, and we became Muslim, then we remained so for a day until evening came, and we left while hiding (4).
Yūnus narrated, from al-Ḥasan:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ṣuhayb is the foremost of the Romans” (5). ⟦2:19⟧
This came with a good chain of transmission (الإسناد) from the hadith of Abū Umāmah, and it came from the hadith of Anas and Umm Hāniʾ (1).
Mujāhid said: The first to make Islam public were seven: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, Bilāl, Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb ..., abridged (2).
Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: The father of Ṣuhayb, or his uncle, was an agent of Khosrow over al-Ubullah, and their dwellings were in the land of Mosul (3), and the Romans raided them and took Ṣuhayb captive while he was a boy, so he grew up among the Romans, then Kalb bought him, and they sold him in Mecca to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān, who freed him.
As for his family, they claim that he fled from the Romans and came to Mecca (4).
Muṣʿab ibn ʿAbd Allāh: عن أبيه، عن ربيعة بن عثمان، عن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه، قال:
I went out with ʿUmar until he entered an orchard of Ṣuhayb.
When Ṣuhayb saw him, he said: O people! O folk!
ʿUmar said: Why does he call to the people?
I said: Rather, it is a servant of his called Yuḥannas (5).
ʿUmar said to him: Were it not for three traits in you, O ⟦2:20⟧
Ṣuhayb ..., the hadith (1).
al-Wāqidī: حدثنا عثمان بن محمد، عن عبد الحكم بن صهيب، عن عمر بن الحكم، قال:
ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir was tortured until he did not know what he was saying, and Ṣuhayb was tortured until he did not know what he was saying, among a group of Muslims, until was revealed: “Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been persecuted” [Qurʾān 16:110] (2).
Mujāhid said: As for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his uncle protected him, and as for Abū Bakr, his people protected him, and the others were seized - he named Ṣuhayb among them - and they dressed them in iron coats of mail and scorched them in the sun until the hardship reached them to the utmost; so they gave them what they asked - meaning: uttering disbelief - and every man's people came with leather mats containing water, and threw them in it, except Bilāl. ⟦2:21⟧
al-Kalbī: from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “And among the people is he who sells himself ...” [Qurʾān 2:207] was revealed about Ṣuhayb and a group of his companions, whom the people of Mecca seized to torture them in order to turn them back to polytheism (1).
Aḥmad in his Musnad: حدثنا أسباط، حدثنا أشعث، عن كردوس، عن ابن مسعود، قال:
The nobles of Quraysh passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and ʿAmmār were with him, and they said: Are you content with these?
Then the Qurʾān was revealed about them: “And warn by it those who fear ...” up to His saying: “and Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers” [Qurʾān 6 (2): 51 - 58].
ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī: from Abū ʿUthmān:
that when Ṣuhayb wanted to emigrate, the people of Mecca said to him: You came to us a poor, insignificant man, and your condition has changed!
He said: What do you think if I leave my wealth, will you let me go on my way?
They said: Yes.
So he handed his wealth over to them.
That reached the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Ṣuhayb has profited! Ṣuhayb has profited!” (3).
Yaʿqūb ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhrī: حدثنا حصين بن حذيفة (4) بن صيفي، حدثنا ⟦2:22⟧ أبي وعمومتي، عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن صهيب، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was shown the abode of your emigration, a salt marsh between two lava fields! It is either Hajar or Yathrib (1).”
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Medina, and I had intended (2) to go out with him, but some young men of Quraysh prevented me, so that night I kept standing up and not sitting down.
They said: Allah has occupied him from you with his stomach - and I was not ill - so they slept, and I went, but some of them caught up with me at a distance of a postal stage.
I said to them: Shall I give you several ounces of gold and you let me go?
They did so, and I said: Dig under the threshold of the door (3), you will find it, and take from so-and-so two robes.
I went out until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Qubāʾ, and when he saw me, he said: “O Abū Yaḥyā, the sale has profited,” three times.
I said: None informed you but Gabriel.
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: حدثنا علي بن زيد، عن ابن المسيب، قال:
Ṣuhayb came as an emigrant, and a group followed him, so he dismounted from his mount and emptied his quiver, and said:
You know that I am among the best of you in archery, and by Allah, you will not reach me until I have shot every arrow I have, then I strike you with my sword; but if you wish, I will show you where my wealth is, and you will let me go on my way?
They said: We will.
When he came to the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The sale has profited, O Abū Yaḥyā!”, and was revealed: “And among the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah” [Qurʾān 2:207] (4). ⟦2:23⟧
Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī said: Ṣuhayb fled from the Romans with wealth and settled in Mecca, and made a pact with Ibn Judʿān; the Romans had taken him only from Nineveh.
ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm ibn Ṣuhayb: عن عمر بن الحكم بن ثوبان، عن صهيب، قال:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Qubāʾ, having developed sore eyes on the way and being hungry, and in front of him were fresh dates, and I fell upon them.
ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah! Do you not see Ṣuhayb eating dates while he has sore eyes?
The Prophet ﷺ said that to me.
I said: I am only eating on the side of my healthy eye, and he smiled (1).
ʿUrwah, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah and others mentioned Ṣuhayb among those who witnessed Badr.
Abū Zurʿah: حدثنا يوسف بن عدي، حدثنا يوسف بن محمد بن يزيد بن صيفي، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن أبي جده، عن صهيب:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him love Ṣuhayb with the love of a mother for her child (2).”
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، عن معاوية بن قرة، عن عائذ بن عمرو: that ⟦2:24⟧ Salmān, Ṣuhayb, and Bilāl were sitting, and Abū Sufyān passed by them, and they said:
The swords of Allah have not yet taken their due from the neck of the enemy of Allah.
Abū Bakr said: Do you say this to the elder of Quraysh and its master?
He said: The Prophet ﷺ was informed of that and said: “O Abū Bakr, perhaps you have angered them; if you have angered them, you have angered your Lord.”
So he went back to them and said: O my brothers, perhaps you are angry?
They said: No, O Abū Bakr, may Allah forgive you (1).
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl: عن حمزة بن صهيب، عن أبيه، قال:
ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb: What a man you are, were it not for three traits in you!
He said: And what are they?
He said: You took a patronymic (الكنية) though you have no child, you claimed descent from the Arabs though you are of the Romans! And there is extravagance in you with food.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me the patronymic (الكنية) Abū Yaḥyā, and I am of al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ; the Romans took me captive from Mosul after I was a boy who knew my lineage; and as for what you said about extravagance with food:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The best of you is he who feeds food (2).”
And Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah narrated: عن يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب، عن أبيه:
that ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb: Were it not for three in you?
Some narrate it omitting: “from his father.”
And he added: Even if a piece of dung were split open for me, I would claim descent to it.
And Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن زيد بن أسلم:
that ʿUmar said to Ṣuhayb: Were it not for three ⟦2:25⟧ traits.
He said: And what are they? By Allah, you never stop finding fault with something.
He said: Your taking a patronymic (الكنية) though you have no child; your claiming descent to al-Namir ibn Qāsiṭ though you are a man with a foreign accent (1); and that you do not hold on to wealth ..., the hadith.
And in it: And a wet nurse was sought for me in al-Ubullah (2), so this is from that.
As for wealth, do you see me spend except in what is right?
And Sālim narrated, from his father:
that ʿUmar said: If something befalls me, let Ṣuhayb lead the people in prayer - three times - then agree upon your affair on the third day.
al-Wāqidī said: Ṣuhayb died in Medina, in Shawwāl, in the year 38, aged 70.
So too said al-Madāʾinī and others about his death.
al-Madāʾinī said: He lived 73 years.
al-Fasawī said: He lived 84 years (may Allah be pleased with him).
He has about thirty hadiths.
Muslim narrated three of them from him (3). ⟦2:26⟧
